title: AI-powered DeterTech cameras may have cut trespass at Dingwall's canal level crossings from about five incidents a day in June 2025
summary: Network Rail reported fewer trespass incidents after installing DeterTech AI cameras at Dingwall, alongside signage and campaigns. It supplied no post-installation count and noted a renewed rise.
account: Network Rail reported on June 9, 2026 that trespass had declined at Dingwall after it installed AI-powered DeterTech cameras. Monitoring in June 2025 had found an average of five incidents a day. The cameras detect people leaving the designated route, sound warnings, and send images to Network Rail and British Transport Police. Signage, safety campaigns, and minor site changes accompanied the installation. The release gives no post-installation count and says that incidents had begun rising again as the weather improved. It does not isolate the cameras’ effect or document an individual alert that prevented an accident.
purpose: The cameras are built to detect people leaving the designated route, warn them and alert Network Rail and police in real time.
system: DeterTech AI-powered cameras with audio warnings and live image relay
deployer: Network Rail (Scotland's Railway) with British Transport Police
taxonomy_note: Fewer trespass incidents after detection and audio warnings are read as a safety mechanism working; trespass is also an offense.

ratings.reason: The release reports a reduction without numbers and notes incidents rising again.
No quantified operational outcome is documented.

ai_role.statement: The release credits the reduction to the cameras together with signage and campaigns. Detection counts, false alarms and responses are not reported. The cameras' AI is described only as detecting route departures.
